scope.program: Troubled Asset Relief Program Capital Purchase Program
scope.primary_transaction: Marshall & Ilsley Corporation CPP investment and Bank of Montreal repayment transaction
scope.question: Did the public receive contractually structured and realized value recovery from capital, authority and risk supplied to private banks, and what does that result not recover?

sources.title: Treasury Announces TARP Capital Purchase Program Description
supports: Treasury purchase of senior preferred shares as Tier 1 capital rather than a grant
five-percent annual dividends for the first five years and nine percent thereafter
warrants to purchase common stock with an aggregate market price equal to fifteen percent of the senior preferred investment for publicly traded institutions
executive-compensation and corporate-governance conditions, including a clawback for materially inaccurate earnings-based incentive compensation
does_not_support: the later realized return
that every participating institution received identical economic terms
public voting control over ordinary bank operations
full recovery of systemic, household or distributional costs

sources.title: Capital Purchase Program Overview
supports: capital supplied to 707 financial institutions in 48 states
Treasury receipt of preferred stock or debt securities rather than grant treatment
five-percent and nine-percent dividend structure for most participants
warrants or other securities designed to let taxpayers receive additional returns as banks recovered
does_not_support: the complete recipient-selection denominator or every rejected applicant
equal benefit to every taxpayer, borrower, worker or homeowner
that taxpayer upside was proportionate to all public risk and externalities
public co-governance over participating banks

sources.title: Treasury Announces Warrant Repurchase and Disposition Process for the Capital Purchase Program
supports: issuer repurchase at fair market value through a contractually defined process
independent-appraiser procedure when Treasury and an issuer could not agree
Treasury use of market, model and third-party inputs to protect taxpayer value
authority to liquidate warrants when the issuer did not repurchase them
does_not_support: that every valuation maximized public return
absence of political, market-timing or information asymmetry
individual taxpayer participation in valuation decisions
the final program-wide return

sources.title: Treasury Releases TARP Warrant Disposition Report
supports: the stated purpose of warrants was additional potential taxpayer return
four billion dollars in gross warrant-disposition proceeds from 34 banks as of December 31, 2009
reported additional absolute return from warrants beyond dividends for that bounded cohort
does_not_support: the eventual return on the entire CPP portfolio
risk-adjusted proportionality
that warrant proceeds reached directly affected households
complete public governance rights

sources.title: $1.7 Billion Additional TARP Funds Returned to Taxpayers, Positive Return on TARP Bank Programs Reaches $10 Billion
supports: Bank of Montreal purchase of 1.715 billion dollars of M&I Bank CPP preferred shares
3.3 million dollars of warrant proceeds and 11.9 million dollars of final accrued dividends
214.6 million dollars of earlier dividends
1.9448 billion dollars in total lifetime taxpayer proceeds against a 1.715 billion dollar original preferred-share purchase
229.8 million dollars in stated positive return for the bounded transaction
does_not_support: the counterfactual failure cost without the investment
a risk-adjusted or social-welfare return calculation
direct household compensation
that all CPP investments produced positive returns

sources.title: Capital Purchase Program Payments
supports: CPP closure by September 30, 2023
226.8 billion dollars recovered through repayments, dividends, interest and other income
204.9 billion dollars initially invested
aggregate positive gross recovery relative to initial investment
does_not_support: net income after Treasury borrowing costs and write-offs by itself
distributional fairness
full TARP profitability
complete recovery of economic crisis costs

sources.title: Troubled Asset Relief Program final financial summary
supports: 204.895 billion dollars disbursed under CPP
199.675 billion dollars in investment repayments
5.220 billion dollars in write-offs and losses
27.106 billion dollars received from investments
5.579 billion dollars in interest expense
16.307 billion dollars in final CPP net income
31.1 billion dollars in net cost across TARP as a whole after interest expense
does_not_support: CPP profit as proof that all TARP programs were profitable
complete social-cost accounting
direct recovery by every affected population
absence of nonfinancial public risk

sources.title: Final Report on the Troubled Asset Relief Program
supports: final CBO estimate of 31 billion dollars in total TARP subsidy cost
substantial financial risk assumed by the federal government
net gains from other transactions with financial institutions through dividends, interest and capital gains
separation of profitable financial-institution transactions from costly housing, AIG and automotive components
does_not_support: Treasury's CPP accounting as a complete measure of social benefit
that all public risk was compensated
a conclusion about bailout justice or necessity
a direct R7 right held by affected households

sources.title: Bank Investment Programs
supports: 245.5 billion dollars invested across five TARP bank programs
275.9 billion dollars recovered through repayments and other income by September 30, 2023
aggregate positive return across the bank-investment-program category
does_not_support: profitability of non-bank TARP programs
equal return from each bank program or recipient
full macroeconomic or distributional accounting
transfer to other public-private sectors without new evidence

sources.title: Capital Purchase Program FAQs
supports: regulator consultation before Treasury accepted a redemption request
issuer right to repurchase warrants only at contractually defined fair market value
Treasury ability to sell warrants to investors if the issuer did not repurchase them
separation of preferred-stock repayment from later warrant disposition
does_not_support: that every redemption preserved maximum public value
public voting control over the recipient
direct citizen participation in administration
the final total return by itself
